plan_a_advantages: More frequent trail running sessions mimic the demands of trail racing.
The lower overall volume and emphasis on easy runs reduces the risk of overtraining and injury.
The shorter, more manageable runs allow for better recovery and adaptation to trail conditions.
plan_b_advantages: Includes strength training, which is beneficial for injury prevention and overall running efficiency.
The longer, dedicated long runs could build a higher level of aerobic capacity, though at the risk of fatigue.
The extended rest days could be beneficial for an athlete who needs more recovery time.
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It prioritizes consistent aerobic work with manageable volume, focusing on building a solid base and trail-specific endurance without excessive fatigue. The shorter, more frequent trail runs, combined with rest days, allow for better recovery and adaptation. Plan B, while including longer runs, dedicates a significant portion of the week to strength training and extended rest, which isn't the most efficient approach for maximizing speed gains in trail running.
